name: Eagle Villas (Eagle Villas Apartments)
headline: Ulysses Development Group bought and renovated Eagle Villas, a 120-unit 1990s tax credit complex of two- to four-bedroom apartments at 405 Nogal Road in the Town of Eagle, to keep it affordable after its old restrictions expired. It won a 2025 federal 4% credit award from CHFA backed by $32M of Eagle County Housing and Development Authority bonds.
why_it_matters: This is a resort-county preservation model. A housing authority bridge loan and a $5M state loan let the developer buy at market price ($39M) under a 90-day deadline. Eleven months later a bond and 4% credit resyndication repaid the bridge money, paid for the renovation and set 60 years of affordability. The housing authority's partner role brings a property tax exemption.

status.label: Renovation complete; grand reopening held 2026-08-11
status.detail: UDG announced its financial closing and resyndication in May 2025. Enterprise dates the bond and equity closing and the start of rehab to June 2025. A grand reopening on 2026-08-11 marked completion of a $12.6M renovation of all 120 apartments.

next_step: Watch for CHFA Form 8609 issuance; the deal should then move to CHFA's placed-in-service list.

key_numbers.meaning: CHFA lists 36 units at 50% AMI, 72 at 60% AMI and 12 at 80% AMI, in 48 two-bedroom, 68 three-bedroom and 4 four-bedroom apartments.
About $27.7M over 10 years; no state credit. National Equity Fund invested $22.9M of equity.
The Eagle County Housing and Development Authority issued the multifamily housing revenue bonds. JPMorgan Chase is the construction ($41.4M) and permanent ($25.4M) lender.
Bought in June 2024 for $39M (about $325,000 a unit). The permanent financing totals $68.8M.

facts.value: Family, acquisition/rehabilitation; in a DDA; not in a QCT or SADDA; Section 8 column marked No
120 total, 120 low-income; about 133,000 sq ft; apartments of 874 to 1,200 sq ft
Built as a LIHTC property in two phases: Phase I of 100 units, completed in 1994 under a 30-year LURA, and Phase II of 20 units, completed in 1997 under a 50-year LURA
Eagle Villas LLC, which acquired the property in 2013; it listed the property for sale in November 2023 and marketed it as a market-rate opportunity
Eagle Villas Owner LP (the tax credit partnership took title at acquisition, 11 months before the bond closing); ECHDA is special limited partner
A new 60-year LURA. ECHDA required it in exchange for its acquisition loan, with rents unchanged

Remodeled kitchens and bathrooms, Energy Star appliances, new flooring, insulation and paint; new siding, windows, roofs and gutters; ADA compliance, LED lighting, rooftop solar and clubhouse improvements

Enterprise's chart puts Eagle Villas rents $459 (2BR), $284 (3BR) and $1,635 (4BR) below Eagle County medians. The county said rents would have had to rise by more than $1,900 a month without the public sources
UDG says Eagle Villas is over half of the affordable housing in the Town of Eagle

background.text: The old restrictions covered 100 of the 120 units and were about to expire (see discrepancies). The owner listed the property in late 2023 as a market-rate conversion. Without a preservation buyer, most units would have gone to market rent.

UDG went under contract in February 2024 and closed the purchase on 2024-06-14 with ECHDA and DOLA. It used a step-in-the-shoes structure, with the future tax credit partnership buying first, to meet the market price and a short closing window.
Northmarq reported the sale at $39 million on 2024-06-19 after a competitive bid process. Enterprise gives the acquisition cost as about $325,000 a unit, consistent with that price.

In 2024 the county said the second closing, with tax-exempt bonds and LIHTC equity, would repay $3.5M of the ECHDA loan and the $5M DOLA loan and fund the renovation; the 2025 and 2026 releases still list a $4M county loan and a $5M DOLA loan in the permanent financing. The county put the cash contributions from equity, DOLA and ECHDA at $35.4M.
Enterprise estimates that building the 120-unit, 133,000 sq ft community new would cost $80-93 million, against $69 million total for the preservation.

discrepancies.text: Sources disagree on when the old restrictions expired: Eagle County said the end of 2024, Northmarq said 2025, and Enterprise said 2026.
Eagle County and the 2026 reopening release describe residents at 45-60% AMI, UDG's 2025 release and Enterprise say 45-80% AMI, and CHFA's award lists 50%, 60% and 80% AMI units.
The renovation budget is given as about $9.5M ($80,000 a unit) by Eagle County, $10M by UDG in 2025, $11.5M by Enterprise and $12.6M (about $104,000 a unit) at the 2026 reopening.
Northmarq dates Phase II to 1997, while Enterprise says the property was built in 1994 and 1996.
The financial closing was announced in May 2025, while Enterprise dates the bond and equity closing to June 2025.
